title: A Day for Kids in the USA
summary: Many kids ride a big yellow bus. At school, they read, write, play and eat lunch with friends.

cover.alt: A boy with curly dark hair, a blue shirt and a yellow backpack eats cereal at a kitchen table. A yellow school bus waits outside the sunlit window.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: What do kids in the USA eat for breakfast? How do they go to school? Many kids ride a big yellow bus. At school, they read, write, play and eat lunch with friends. After school, they play and do homework. Let's read about breakfast, school, games and dinner.

items.prompt: What do you eat for breakfast?
How do you go to school?
What is your favorite class at school?

blocks.title: Part 1: Morning at Home and the Trip to School
paragraphs: It is seven o'clock in the morning. A clock rings. Children wake up and get out of bed. They wash their face and put on their clothes. Then they brush their teeth.

Now it is time for breakfast. Children eat cereal with milk, or eggs and toast. They put the cereal in a bowl and add milk. Toast is hot, brown bread. Fruit is good for breakfast too. Children eat a banana or an apple. They drink orange juice or milk. Breakfast gives them food before a busy day at school.
After breakfast, children get their school bag. It is called a backpack. They put in books, pencils and a water bottle. They can put a lunch box in too. Now they are ready to go.

Children go to school by bus or by car. They can walk too. The yellow school bus stops near their home. Children get on the bus and sit with friends. They look out of the window. The bus arrives at school. Children get off and say hello to their teacher.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: Morning at Home and the Trip to School

items.prompt: How do many children in the USA go to school?
items.answer: Many children ride a yellow school bus. Some children walk, and some children go by car.

blocks.title: Part 2: Morning Classes and Lunch
paragraphs: Children go into their classroom. They say hello to their friends. They put their bags away and sit at their desks.

First, they have reading. The teacher reads a story to the class. Children listen and look at the book. Then they read too. They read alone or in small groups. They talk about the story with their teacher.

Next is writing. The teacher walks around and helps the children. Then they have math. They work with numbers. They add and take away. They use blocks and pictures too. The teacher writes on the board. Children put a hand up to ask a question.
After class, it is time to play. This time is called recess. Children go outside. They run, jump and play games with friends.

Then it is time for lunch. The school has a big eating room called the cafeteria. It has long tables and many chairs. Children sit and eat with friends. They bring lunch from home or get school lunch. A lunch box can have a sandwich, an apple or cheese. School lunch can be pizza, chicken, rice, salad or fruit. Many children drink milk. School meals can be free.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: Morning Classes and Lunch

items.prompt: Where do many children eat lunch, and what can they eat?
items.answer: Many children eat lunch in the cafeteria with friends. They can eat a sandwich from home, or a school lunch like pizza, chicken or salad.

rows.meaning: Use it at a table with free chairs. It is a polite way to join people.
rows.example: Can I sit here? This chair is free.

rows.term: What do you have for lunch?
rows.meaning: Use it to ask a friend about their food.
rows.example: What do you have for lunch today?

rows.term: I have a sandwich and an apple.
rows.meaning: Use it to talk about your food. Change the food words.
rows.example: I have rice and an orange.

blocks.title: Part 3: Afternoon Classes and Going Home
paragraphs: After lunch, classes start again. Children have more to learn and do. There is time for art, music, games and science.
In art class, children draw pictures. They paint with many colors. They cut paper and make things. They show their pictures to the teacher.
In music class, children sing songs together. They listen to music and play small drums or bells.
PE is sports class. Children go to a big room for games. They run, throw balls and play in teams. They can play outside too.
In science class, children learn about water and small animals. They look at pictures and ask questions. The teacher helps them find answers.
At the end of the day, children clean the classroom. They put their books away and clean their desks. They get their bags and coats. Now it is time to go home.
The school day ends in the afternoon. Children go home on the yellow bus, walk with a parent or go by car. They say bye to their teacher and friends.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: Afternoon Classes and Going Home

items.prompt: What do children do at the end of the school day?
items.answer: They put books away, clean their desks, get their bags and go home.

blocks.title: Part 4: After School
paragraphs: Children are hungry after school. At home, they eat a snack. A snack is a little food between meals. It can be an apple, cheese or a cookie. They drink water or milk.
Then it is time for homework. Homework is school work at home. Children read a little book or answer math questions. A parent can help. Children put their books away when they finish.
After that, there is time to play. Children go outside with friends. They ride bikes and play ball. They play in the yard or at the park. A yard is the grass next to a house.
Children can do activities after school too. They play soccer, basketball or baseball. They go to music or art class. They can join a club with other children who like the same things.

An after-school program is a place to go after class. Children get help with reading and math there. They play games too. After school is also a time to see grandparents, brothers, sisters and friends.

items.prompt: What can children do after school?
items.answer: They can eat a snack, do homework and play outside. They can also play sports, go to a club or visit family.

rows.meaning: Use it to ask how a friend goes to school.
rows.example: Do you ride the bus or walk?

rows.term: What do you do after school?
rows.meaning: Use it to ask about a friend's afternoon.
rows.example: What do you do after school on Mondays?

rows.meaning: Use it when you leave a friend. You meet them again soon.
rows.example: Bye, Tom! See you in class!

blocks.title: Part 5: Dinner, Bed and the Weekend
paragraphs: In the evening, the family eats dinner. Dinner can be chicken, rice or soup with vegetables. Children sit at the table and talk about their day. They talk about school, friends and games.
Children help at home too. They put things on the table for dinner. After dinner, they help clean the table. They give food to the dog or the cat.
Then there is free time. Children play with toys, draw or watch TV. They can play video games too.
Before bed, children wash. They take a bath or a shower. They put on clean clothes for bed. Then they brush their teeth again.
A parent reads a story. Children listen in bed and look at the pictures in the book. Then they say good night. The lights go off. It is time to sleep.
On the weekend, there is no school. Children can sleep a little longer. They play, see family and go to sports games.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Dinner, Bed and the Weekend

items.prompt: What do many children do before bed?
items.answer: They take a bath or a shower, put on clean clothes and brush their teeth. Many parents read them a story.

blocks.title: Scene: Lunch with a New Friend in the Cafeteria
paragraphs: You visit a school in the USA for one day. It is lunchtime. You walk into the big, loud cafeteria with your lunch box. A girl named Mia sits at a long table. There is a free chair next to her.
Your goal is to sit with Mia, talk about lunch and after school, and say goodbye at the end of lunch.

images.alt: In a busy school cafeteria, a girl in a green shirt smiles and gestures toward an empty chair beside her. A boy with curly dark hair, a blue shirt and a yellow backpack approaches carrying a green lunch box.

blocks.title: Conversation: Lunch with a New Friend in the Cafeteria

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi! Can I sit here?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Sure! Sit next to me. I'm Mia.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. I'm from Japan. I'm here for one day.

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Wow, Japan! Welcome to our school. Do you like it?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes! I like recess. We ran and played tag.

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Me too. Recess is my favorite. What do you have for lunch?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I have rice balls and some fruit. What about you?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: I have a sandwich and an apple. My mom makes it. Sometimes I get school lunch. Today it is pizza.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Pizza at school? That's cool. At my school in Japan, we eat in our classroom.

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Really? Here we eat in the cafeteria. It is big and loud!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, it is very loud! Do you ride the bus?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Yes, I ride the yellow bus. My stop is near my house. How do you go to school?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I walk to school with my friends. What do you do after school?

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: First, I eat a snack. Then I do my homework. On Tuesdays, I play soccer.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I play soccer too!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Great! Maybe we can play soccer in PE this afternoon.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I hope so!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: Oh, that's the bell. Lunch is over. Put your trash here.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Okay. Thank you, Mia. See you in class!

turns.speaker: Mia
turns.text: See you in class! Let's go.

blocks.title: Speaking
paragraphs: Tell a partner about your day. Use short sentences, from morning to night.
1. Say what time you wake up and what you eat for breakfast.
2. Say how you go to school.
3. Name your classes in the morning and the afternoon.
4. Say what you eat for lunch and where you eat it.
5. Say what you do after school and before bed.
Then ask your partner the same questions. Find two things that are the same in your days. Find one thing that is different from a day in the USA.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: Kids in the USA eat, learn and play. They have breakfast, go to school and eat lunch with friends. After school, there is time for homework and games. The day ends with dinner and a story.

items.prompt: Which American breakfast do you want to try?
Do you want to ride a yellow school bus? Why?
Which part of the American school day do you like best?
What do you do after school that American kids do too?
